entries.subject: SDSS DR9 color HiPS
entries.finding: A 3000 x 3000 px hips2fits cutout of CDS/P/SDSS9/color, 20 arcmin wide at the survey's 0.4 arcsec per pixel. The bar and the star-forming centre are not saturated. Shallow: the outer arms are faint.

entries.subject: DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR9 and DR10 color composites
entries.finding: Looked at as 700 px previews on 2026-10-01. The DR10 color HiPS has a purple band of corrupt coadd across the southern half of the disc. The DR9 viewer cutout is clean and deeper than SDSS, but its display stretch saturates the bar and the inner disc to white.
entries.revisitWhen: A Legacy Surveys composite with an unsaturated centre is published, or the bake composes two images as M31's does.

entries.subject: Pan-STARRS DR1 color HiPS
entries.finding: Its sky subtraction leaves dark blocks across and around the disc (700 px preview, 2026-10-01).

entries.subject: Observatory press images of NGC 2903
entries.finding: The NOIRLab and ESO image archives return no photograph of NGC 2903. ESA/Hubble's potw2143a (5903 x 3959 px) and heic0102a cover the inner disc only.
entries.revisitWhen: A whole-disc photograph is published under an attribution licence.

entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC2903, model _bdbarf: a Sérsic bulge (7.1% of the light, magnitude 11.225, half-light radius 7.29″ = 0.32 kpc, n = 0.496, axis ratio 0.523, PA 17.27°) and an exponential disc (90.1% of the light, scale length 54.89″ = 2.44 kpc, axis ratio 0.487, PA 19.57°, face-on central surface brightness 19.162, 18.381 as projected on the sky) and a Ferrers bar (2.7% of the light, radius 71.25″ = 3.16 kpc, axis ratio 0.189, PA 30.89°, central surface brightness 19.770 on the sky). Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 17.236 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 65° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.34).
